body: This is fairly pervasive, we can't mute our way out of it. Does that mean it's a `blocker`? Certainly needs fairly urgent attention IMO.
If this is urgent @DaveCTurner , I can take a look at it to see if I can somehow handle it in a manageable timeframe.

Thanks Iraklis; I suspect we don't _need_ to assert this here, but still it indicates we're in a surprising state and I'd like to understand why before just suppressing it. Presumably we're completing the cluster state update (which leads to calling `PeerFinder#closePeers`) before calling `PeerFinder#deactivate`? Or maybe we became LEADER and then CANDIDATE again straight away and then the cluster state update completes? Somewhat surprising that this doesn't seem to reproduce in `CoordinatorTests` too.

Ah I think I see it, this looks suspicious:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d411acecbcbd029ebadbfa533a07c70330d454c8/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L417-L421

We need to check `mode` and call `PeerFinder#closePeers` in the same `synchronized` block I reckon. If not, we could indeed fall back to `CANDIDATE` and reactivate the `PeerFinder` before we get around to closing it. That's not something the `CoordinatorTests` would catch because they're single-threaded.
Thanks for the hints @DaveCTurner ! I can follow up with seeing if I can create a test to reproduce this and fix the synchronized block.
